course.introMd:
This course teaches what the GRE General Test measures, one idea per lesson. Each lesson explains the concept, works original examples step by step, shows the traps that cost marks, and ends with a short check whose answers stay hidden until you open them.

### The test in brief

The current GRE General Test takes about 1 hour and 58 minutes. It opens with one 30-minute Analytical Writing task ("Analyze an Issue"), followed by two Verbal Reasoning sections (12 questions in 18 minutes, then 15 in 23) and two Quantitative Reasoning sections (12 in 21 minutes, then 15 in 26). The Verbal and Quantitative sections can come in any order after the essay. Each measure is adaptive by section: how you do in its first section sets the difficulty of its second. Verbal and Quantitative are scored from 130 to 170, Analytical Writing from 0 to 6 in half points, and nothing is subtracted for a wrong answer, so never leave a question blank. A basic on-screen calculator is available in Quantitative Reasoning only.

### How to use the course

Work through a unit in order: the lessons build on each other. After each lesson, take the check before you open the answers, then use the practice link to apply the idea on fresh questions. Every question in this course is original and written for UniExamer; none comes from ETS, and difficulty is our editorial judgement, not a calibrated GRE level.

units.title: Getting started
units.summary: How the GRE General Test is built: the five sections and their timings, how the second section of each measure adapts to the first, how navigation inside a section works, and how Verbal, Quant and the essay are scored. Read this first; every later lesson assumes it.

lessons.title: How the GRE works: sections, timing, adaptivity and scoring
lessons.summary: Know the five sections, the time per question, how section-level adaptivity works and why you should never leave a GRE question blank.

units.title: Text Completion
units.summary: Text Completion questions give one to five sentences with one to three blanks, and credit only a fully correct set of answers. This unit teaches how to find the clue for a blank, read the signal words that set its direction, work through two- and three-blank passages, and use vocabulary precisely in context.

lessons.title: Text Completion: reading for the clue
lessons.summary: Find the words in the sentence that decide the blank, predict your own answer before you look, and only then match it to a choice.

lessons.title: Text Completion: signal words that set the direction
lessons.summary: Use contrast, continuation, cause and time words to know whether the blank agrees with its clue or opposes it, and handle double reversals.

lessons.title: Text Completion: two and three blanks
lessons.summary: Start with the blank that has the strongest clue, let each answer inform the next, and test the whole passage before you commit.

lessons.title: Text Completion: vocabulary in context
lessons.summary: Handle second meanings, misleading roots and words with the right sense but the wrong charge, and decide what to do with a word you do not know.

units.title: Sentence Equivalence
units.summary: Sentence Equivalence questions give one sentence with one blank and six choices, and ask for the two choices that complete it with sentences alike in meaning; both must be right to score. This unit teaches a method for finding the pair, how to tell true pairs from near misses, and how to match the tone and strength the sentence asks for.

lessons.title: Sentence Equivalence: a method that finds the pair
lessons.summary: Predict the blank, find every choice that fits, then keep only the two that give sentences alike in meaning. One perfect word without a partner is not enough.

lessons.title: Sentence Equivalence: true pairs and near misses
lessons.summary: Tell a true pair from a near miss: words that share a topic, overlap only in part, or carry a different charge do not give sentences alike in meaning.

lessons.title: Sentence Equivalence: tone and intensity
lessons.summary: Match the strength and tone the sentence asks for: words like only, utterly and nothing short of decide between pairs that point the same way.

units.title: Reading Comprehension
units.summary: About half of GRE Verbal Reasoning is based on passages. This unit teaches how to read a passage for its structure, answer main-idea, detail and inference questions, handle the select-one-or-more and Select-in-Passage formats, and reason about arguments: their assumptions, and what would strengthen, weaken or explain them.

lessons.title: Reading a passage for its structure
lessons.summary: Read each GRE passage for what its parts are doing, not for every fact, and build a quick map you can answer most questions from.

lessons.title: Main idea, primary purpose and the author’s attitude
lessons.summary: State a passage’s main idea in one sentence, match purpose choices verb first, and rule out choices that are too broad, too narrow or off in tone.

lessons.title: Detail and inference questions
lessons.summary: Answer detail questions by going back to the text, and inference questions by taking the smallest step the passage forces, never a step it only allows.

lessons.title: Select-in-Passage and select-one-or-more questions
lessons.summary: Judge each choice of a select-one-or-more question on its own, and find a Select-in-Passage sentence by turning the description into a test.

lessons.title: Argument passages: conclusions, assumptions and flaws
lessons.summary: Break a short argument into conclusion and evidence, find the unstated assumption that links them, and name the flaw when the link fails.

lessons.title: Strengthen, weaken and explain
lessons.summary: Use the gap in an argument to find what strengthens or weakens it, and resolve an apparent paradox with the fact that lets both sides be true.

units.title: Quantitative question types
units.summary: GRE Quantitative Reasoning uses four formats: quantitative comparison, multiple choice with one answer, multiple choice with one or more answers, and numeric entry. This unit teaches the strategy each format needs, apart from the maths itself, which the following units cover topic by topic.

lessons.title: Quantitative comparison: strategy for the four fixed choices
lessons.summary: Compare two quantities without computing more than you must: simplify both sides safely, test deliberate cases, and know when the answer is fixed.

lessons.title: Numeric entry and select-one-or-more questions
lessons.summary: Answer numeric entry questions with no choices to lean on, and test every choice of a select-one-or-more question against one simplified condition.

units.title: Arithmetic
units.summary: Arithmetic is one of the four content areas of GRE Quantitative Reasoning. This unit covers the integer properties (divisibility, primes, remainders, odd and even), exponents and roots, fractions, decimals and the number line, percent, ratio, rate and sequences of numbers, with the traps each topic sets.

lessons.title: Integers, divisibility and primes
lessons.summary: Break any integer into primes, then use the factorisation to count divisors, find the GCD and LCM, and decide what must divide a number.

lessons.title: Remainders, odd and even, and positive and negative
lessons.summary: Write any remainder as an equation, work out remainders of sums and products, and settle odd, even and sign questions by rule, not by guessing.

lessons.title: Exponents and roots
lessons.summary: Use the exponent rules on a common base, simplify and combine square roots, and compare powers without working out huge numbers.

lessons.title: Fractions, decimals and the number line
lessons.summary: Compare and convert fractions and decimals, tell terminating from repeating decimals, and place, measure and divide distances on the number line.

lessons.title: Percents, percent change and successive changes
lessons.summary: Turn every percent into a multiplier, find the right base for a percent change, and chain or undo changes without the classic GRE slips.

lessons.title: Ratios and proportions
lessons.summary: Turn a ratio into parts with one multiplier, link ratios through a shared term, and solve proportions and changing-ratio problems cleanly.

lessons.title: Rates, work and speed
lessons.summary: Use amount = rate × time for distance and work, find true average speeds, add rates for joint work, and keep units straight.

lessons.title: Sequences of numbers
lessons.summary: Find any term of an arithmetic or geometric sequence, count and add terms without off-by-one errors, and handle recursive and repeating patterns.

units.title: Algebra
units.summary: Algebra is one of the four content areas of GRE Quantitative Reasoning. This unit covers linear equations and systems, expressions and factoring, quadratic equations, inequalities and absolute value, functions and invented operations, lines on the coordinate plane, and turning word problems into equations.

lessons.title: Linear equations and systems of two equations
lessons.summary: Solve linear equations without sign slips, solve two-equation systems by substitution or elimination, and spot when only a combination is needed.

lessons.title: Algebraic expressions, identities and factoring
lessons.summary: Expand and factor expressions with three key identities, simplify fractions by cancelling factors, and use identities to evaluate without solving.

lessons.title: Quadratic equations: factoring, the formula and the discriminant
lessons.metaTitle: Quadratic equations: factoring, formula and discriminant
lessons.summary: Solve quadratics by factoring or by the formula, keep both roots, read the discriminant, and use the sum and product of roots as a shortcut.

lessons.title: Inequalities and absolute value
lessons.summary: Solve linear inequalities, flip the sign only when you should, combine ranges correctly, and treat absolute value as distance on the number line.

lessons.title: Functions and invented operations
lessons.summary: Evaluate functions and compositions with careful substitution, solve for an input, and work any operation a question defines with a new symbol.

lessons.title: Coordinate geometry: lines, slopes and intercepts
lessons.summary: Find slopes and intercepts, write the equation of a line, use parallel and perpendicular slopes, and find midpoints and distances on the plane.

lessons.title: Turning word problems into equations
lessons.summary: Name the unknown precisely, translate the words into an equation phrase by phrase, solve it, and answer the question that was actually asked.

units.title: Geometry
units.summary: Geometry is one of the four content areas of GRE Quantitative Reasoning. This unit covers lines and angles, triangles and the Pythagorean theorem, special right triangles and similar figures, circles, quadrilaterals and other polygons, and three-dimensional figures. Every figure is described in words, and each lesson shows how to read a figure for what it states rather than what it appears to show.

lessons.title: Lines and angles: vertical angles, parallels and transversals
lessons.metaTitle: Lines and angles: vertical angles, parallels, transversals
lessons.summary: Find unknown angles from straight lines, crossing lines and parallels cut by a transversal, and read a figure for what it states, not what it looks like.

lessons.title: Triangles and the Pythagorean theorem
lessons.summary: Bound a missing side with the triangle inequality, find areas with the right height, and use the Pythagorean theorem only where it applies.

lessons.title: Special right triangles, similarity and congruence
lessons.summary: Use the 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 side ratios on sight, match similar triangles by their angles, and scale lengths and areas correctly.

lessons.title: Circles: arcs, sectors, inscribed angles and tangents
lessons.summary: Work from the radius to circumference, area, arcs and sectors, and use inscribed angles and tangents to turn circle questions into triangle questions.

lessons.title: Quadrilaterals, polygons, area and perimeter
lessons.summary: Know what each quadrilateral guarantees, find any polygon's angles, and compute areas of trapezoids, parallelograms and composite shapes.

lessons.title: Three-dimensional figures: volume, surface area and diagonals
lessons.metaTitle: Three-dimensional figures: volume, surface area, diagonals
lessons.summary: Find volumes and surface areas of boxes, cubes, cylinders and prisms, scale them correctly, and count how many objects really fit inside.

units.title: Data analysis
units.summary: Data analysis is one of the four content areas of GRE Quantitative Reasoning. This unit covers descriptive statistics (centre, spread, quartiles and boxplots), reading tables and graphs, counting methods, probability, and distributions including the normal curve. Inferential statistics is not tested, so the focus is on reading data accurately and reasoning about it.

lessons.title: Mean, median, mode and range
lessons.summary: Work with sums instead of averages, find the median of any list or frequency table, and predict how centre and spread react to changes in the data.

lessons.title: Standard deviation, quartiles and boxplots
lessons.summary: Judge spread without long calculations: what standard deviation measures, how to find quartiles and the IQR, and what a boxplot can and cannot tell you.

lessons.title: Reading graphs and data interpretation
lessons.summary: Read tables, bar, line and circle graphs, scatterplots and frequency distributions accurately, and answer data interpretation questions with the right base.

lessons.title: Counting: permutations, combinations and Venn diagrams
lessons.summary: Count arrangements and selections with the multiplication principle, decide when order matters, handle restrictions, and count overlapping groups.

lessons.title: Probability: compound events and conditional probability
lessons.summary: Find probabilities by counting, combine events with "and", "or" and "not", draw without replacement, and read conditional probabilities from a two-way table.

lessons.title: Distributions, expected value and the normal curve
lessons.summary: Read a probability distribution, find an expected value, and use the approximate 68–95–99.7 rule and standard units to answer normal-curve questions.

units.title: Analytical Writing: the Issue task
units.summary: The GRE opens with one 30-minute "Analyze an Issue" task, scored from 0 to 6 in half points. These lessons cover what the task asks, how to plan a qualified position with reasons and examples, and how to write and revise it in the time.

lessons.title: The Issue task: what it asks and how it is scored
lessons.summary: What the 30-minute "Analyze an Issue" task asks of you, what ETS says about its scoring, and what a position worth defending looks like.

lessons.title: Planning an Issue essay in five minutes
lessons.summary: Test the statement on cases to find your qualified position, then choose reasons, specific examples and the objection you will answer.

lessons.title: Writing and revising the Issue essay under time
lessons.summary: Write a direct introduction, build body paragraphs that argue, and spend the last minutes on the fixes that change what the essay says.

course.introMd:
This course teaches the three sections of the GMAT exam, one idea per lesson. Each lesson explains the concept, works original examples step by step, shows the traps that cost marks, and ends with a short check whose answers stay hidden until you open them.

### The test in brief

GMAC now calls the exam simply the GMAT exam; it is the format introduced as the GMAT Focus Edition. It has three sections of 45 minutes each, 2 hours 15 minutes in all: Quantitative Reasoning (21 questions), Verbal Reasoning (23) and Data Insights (20). You choose the order of the sections, and you may take one optional 10-minute break. Questions are chosen one at a time according to how you are doing, and within each section you can change up to three answers. There is no calculator in Quantitative Reasoning; Data Insights has an on-screen calculator. Each section is scored from 60 to 90 and the total from 205 to 805, with the three sections weighted equally.

Quantitative Reasoning is problem solving in arithmetic and algebra. Verbal Reasoning is reading comprehension and critical reasoning. Data Insights has five question types: data sufficiency, multi-source reasoning, table analysis, graphics interpretation and two-part analysis.

### How to use the course

Work through a unit in order. After each lesson, take the check before you open the answers, then use the practice link to apply the idea on fresh questions. Every question in this course is original and written for UniExamer; none comes from GMAC, and difficulty is our editorial judgement, not a calibrated GMAT level.

course.introMd:
This course teaches every area of the Online Bocconi Test used for admission to Bocconi's bachelor's programmes, one idea per lesson. Each lesson explains the concept, works original examples step by step, shows the traps that cost marks, and ends with a short check whose answers stay hidden until you open them.

### The test in brief

The standard Online Bocconi Test has 50 multiple-choice questions in 75 minutes, taken online in Italian or English: 24 in mathematics, 11 in reading comprehension, 6 in numerical reasoning and 9 in critical thinking. The areas are mixed together rather than timed separately. Questions come three to a screen, and once you move to the next screen you cannot go back. Calculators are not allowed. A correct answer scores 1 point, a blank 0, a wrong answer −0.2, and a wrong answer to a three-option critical thinking question −0.33. Bocconi does not consider a score below 17.

Applicants to Law and Global Law take a separate Law version with a different mix (5 mathematics, 11 reading, 6 numerical reasoning, 18 logic and critical thinking and 10 verbal reasoning). This course follows the standard test; its reading, numerical reasoning and critical thinking lessons are useful for both.

### How to use the course

The mathematics units are the largest because mathematics is almost half the test. The mind map below shows the whole course at a glance, and the last unit, Quick revision, condenses it into tables, rules and drills for the final weeks. Work through a unit in order, take each check before you open the answers, and use the practice link to apply the idea on fresh questions. Every question in this course is original and written for UniExamer; none comes from Bocconi, and difficulty is our editorial judgement.

course.description: A free course for the Online Bocconi Test for MSc and MA applicants: verbal reasoning, data insight and quantitative reasoning, with worked examples.
course.introMd:
This course teaches the three areas of the Online Bocconi Test that international applicants take for Bocconi's Master of Science and MA programmes, one idea per lesson. Each lesson explains the concept, works original examples step by step, shows the traps that cost marks, and ends with a short check whose answers stay hidden until you open them. The mind map below shows the whole test at a glance.

### The test in brief

The test has 50 multiple-choice questions in 75 minutes: 24 in verbal reasoning, 16 in data insight and 10 in quantitative reasoning, mixed together by topic and difficulty. It is taken online, in Italian or English, and recorded for review. According to Bocconi's rules for the 2027/28 test, questions come three to a screen, you cannot go back to an earlier screen, and calculators are not allowed. A correct answer scores 1 point, a blank 0 and a wrong answer −0.25 (or −0.33 on some questions, which Bocconi does not name). Bocconi does not consider a score below 15 out of 50, and you can sit the test at most three times a year. Applicants to PPA and GLOBE need no test, and Bocconi accepts the GMAT or GRE instead of its own test.

Bocconi describes verbal reasoning as reading comprehension, data and statements, and critical reasoning; data insight as questions on tables and graphs and data sufficiency; and quantitative reasoning as problems using basic mathematics.

### How to use the course

Start with the two getting-started lessons, then work through the areas in any order. The last unit, Beyond basic maths, is optional: it covers derivatives and hypothesis tests, topics that appeared in a 2024 Bocconi sample but that the current test page does not mention. Take each check before you open the answers, and use the practice link to apply the idea on fresh questions. Every question in this course is original and written for UniExamer; none comes from Bocconi, and difficulty is our editorial judgement.

course.introMd:
The TOLC-F has five main sections with separate clocks: Biology has 15 questions in 20 minutes, Chemistry 15 in 20, Mathematics 7 in 12, Physics 7 in 12 and Logic 6 in 8. That is 50 questions in 72 minutes. English follows as a separately scored section of 30 questions in 15 minutes; this course covers the five main sections.

Each question has five options and one correct answer. A correct answer scores 1 point, an unanswered question 0 and a wrong answer −0.25. Calculation aids are not allowed. Once a section closes you cannot return to it. CISIA does not publish the rule for changing answers within an open section. Each university sets its own admission requirements and thresholds: read your programme's admission notice.

Choose a unit, attempt its worked examples on paper, and then solve its short check before opening the solutions. The practice link takes you to the corresponding topic. All course examples and questions are original. The TOLC-F question bank is public, but this material is not drawn from it. Some shared mathematics and science lessons also appear in our TOLC-I course.

course.title: IMAT medicine admission test course
course.metaTitle: Free interactive IMAT course in English and Italian
course.description: Study every IMAT area, from biology and chemistry to physics, maths and logic, with worked examples, instant-feedback checks and flashcards.
course.introMd:
The IMAT is the admission test for the English-taught degrees in Medicine and Surgery, Dentistry and Veterinary Medicine at Italian universities. For 2026/27 it was one paper test of 60 questions in 100 minutes, in English: Reading skills and knowledge acquired in studies 4, Logical reasoning and problems 5, Biology 23, Chemistry 15, and Physics and mathematics 13. Every question has five options and one correct answer. A correct answer scores 1.5 points, a blank 0 and a wrong answer −0.4, for a maximum of 90. EU candidates, and non-EU candidates resident in Italy, need at least 20 points to be placed in the national ranking; admission then depends on the ranking against the places at each university. No calculator is allowed. The rules for 2027/28 had not been published when this course was written; check the new decree when it appears.

The course follows the published syllabus area by area, with the most lessons where the most questions are. Every lesson is interactive: try each worked example before revealing its next step, answer the check questions to see at once whether you were right and why each wrong option is wrong, then fix the facts with the flashcard deck. Mark a lesson complete and the course page keeps your progress in this browser.

Every lesson is also available in Italian. The test itself is only in English, so the Italian lessons keep the key English terms beside the Italian ones. All examples and questions are original and written for this course.

it.introMd:
L’IMAT è il test di ammissione ai corsi di laurea in lingua inglese in Medicina e Chirurgia, Odontoiatria e Medicina Veterinaria delle università italiane. Per il 2026/27 è stato un’unica prova su carta di 60 domande in 100 minuti, in inglese: competenze di lettura e conoscenze acquisite negli studi 4, ragionamento logico e problemi 5, biologia 23, chimica 15, fisica e matematica 13. Ogni domanda ha cinque opzioni e una sola risposta corretta. Una risposta esatta vale 1,5 punti, una omessa 0 e una errata −0,4, per un massimo di 90. I candidati UE, e i candidati non UE residenti in Italia, devono ottenere almeno 20 punti per entrare nella graduatoria nazionale; l’ammissione dipende poi dalla posizione in graduatoria rispetto ai posti di ciascuna università. Non è ammessa la calcolatrice. Le regole per il 2027/28 non erano ancora state pubblicate quando è stato scritto questo corso: controlla il nuovo decreto quando uscirà.

Il corso segue il programma ufficiale area per area, con più lezioni dove ci sono più domande. Ogni lezione è interattiva: prova ogni esempio svolto prima di scoprire il passaggio successivo, rispondi alle domande di verifica per sapere subito se hai ragione e perché ogni opzione sbagliata è sbagliata, poi fissa i concetti con il mazzo di flashcard. Segna una lezione come completata e la pagina del corso terrà traccia dei tuoi progressi in questo browser.

Il test si svolge solo in inglese: per questo le lezioni in italiano riportano accanto ai termini italiani quelli inglesi che troverai nella prova. Ogni lezione esiste anche in inglese. Tutti gli esempi e le domande sono originali e scritti per questo corso.

lessons.summary: Classificare le mutazioni per effetto, spiegare selezione e deriva, usare Hardy-Weinberg e collocare gli organismi nella gerarchia tassonomica.

lessons.title: Tessuti, circolazione e respirazione
lessons.summary: I quattro tipi di tessuto, il percorso del sangue nel cuore e nei due circuiti, la ventilazione, gli scambi gassosi e il trasporto di O₂ e CO₂.

lessons.title: Sistema nervoso, endocrino e immunitario
lessons.summary: Come funzionano impulso nervoso e sinapsi, come ormoni e feedback negativo regolano il corpo, come lo difendono immunità innata e adattativa.

lessons.title: Apparato digerente ed escretore
lessons.summary: Seguire il cibo nella digestione e nell'assorbimento e il filtrato nel nefrone, e prevedere che cosa cambia se mancano un enzima, la bile o l'ADH.

lessons.title: Riproduzione e sviluppo umano
lessons.summary: Gametogenesi, ormoni del ciclo mestruale, fecondazione, impianto e primo sviluppo, con i circuiti di feedback che li collegano.

units.title: Chimica
units.summary: Le 15 domande di chimica: atomo e tavola periodica, legami, nomenclatura, stechiometria e soluzioni, equilibrio, acidi e basi, ossidoriduzioni e chimica organica.

lessons.title: Struttura atomica e configurazione elettronica
lessons.summary: Conta protoni, neutroni ed elettroni di qualsiasi atomo o ione e scrivi le configurazioni elettroniche, anche degli ioni dei metalli di transizione.

lessons.title: Le proprietà periodiche
lessons.summary: Prevedi raggio atomico e ionico, energia di ionizzazione ed elettronegatività dalla posizione di un elemento, e spiega le eccezioni più chieste.

lessons.title: Legami chimici e geometria molecolare
lessons.summary: Distingui legame ionico, covalente e metallico, prevedi la forma delle molecole con la VSEPR e stabilisci se una molecola è polare.

lessons.title: Forze intermolecolari, stati della materia e gas
lessons.summary: Ordina i punti di ebollizione in base alle forze intermolecolari, spiega i passaggi di stato e usa le leggi dei gas e pV = nRT senza calcolatrice.

lessons.title: Nomenclatura inorganica
lessons.summary: Dai nome e formula a ossidi, anidridi, idrossidi, acidi e sali, con la nomenclatura IUPAC e tradizionale, partendo dai numeri di ossidazione.

lessons.title: La mole e la stechiometria
lessons.summary: Passa da massa a moli e a numero di particelle, usa le equazioni bilanciate per quantità che reagiscono e reagente limitante, e ricava formule minime.

lessons.title: Soluzioni, concentrazione e proprietà colligative
lessons.summary: Molarità, diluizioni e molalità; prevedere punto di ebollizione, punto di congelamento e osmosi contando le particelle disciolte.

lessons.title: Velocità di reazione ed equilibrio chimico
lessons.summary: Che cosa accelera una reazione, la legge cinetica ricavata dai dati, la costante di equilibrio e gli spostamenti secondo Le Châtelier.

lessons.title: Acidi, basi, pH e soluzioni tampone
lessons.summary: Riconoscere acidi, basi e coppie coniugate, calcolare il pH con le potenze di dieci senza calcolatrice, prevedere il pH dei sali e capire i tamponi.

lessons.title: Reazioni redox e numeri di ossidazione
lessons.summary: Assegnare i numeri di ossidazione, riconoscere chi si ossida e chi si riduce, bilanciare le redox con le semireazioni e usare i potenziali standard.

lessons.title: Composti organici e gruppi funzionali
lessons.summary: Riconoscere le famiglie di idrocarburi e i gruppi funzionali, dare il nome ai composti semplici e spiegarne ebollizione, solubilità e acidità.

lessons.title: Isomeria e reazioni organiche
lessons.summary: Isomeri strutturali, geometrici e ottici, centri chirali, e i prodotti di addizione, sostituzione, ossidazione ed esterificazione.

units.title: Fisica
units.summary: La parte di fisica delle 13 domande di fisica e matematica: cinematica, dinamica, energia, fluidi, termodinamica, elettricità e magnetismo, tutto senza calcolatrice.

lessons.title: Unità di misura, vettori e cinematica
lessons.summary: Unità SI e prefissi, somma e scomposizione dei vettori, equazioni del moto uniformemente accelerato e caduta libera, tutto senza calcolatrice.

lessons.title: Forze e leggi di Newton
lessons.summary: Le tre leggi di Newton, i diagrammi delle forze, attrito, piani inclinati, ascensori e moto circolare: ogni problema di forze ridotto a F = ma.

lessons.title: Lavoro, energia e quantità di moto
lessons.summary: Lavoro, energia cinetica e potenziale, potenza e quantità di moto: quando si conserva l'energia, quando la quantità di moto, e come usarle.

lessons.title: Fluidi, pressione e galleggiamento
lessons.summary: Densità, pressione e profondità, principi di Pascal e di Archimede e flusso nei condotti: la fisica dei fluidi dietro galleggiamento, idraulica e flebo.

lessons.title: Calore, leggi dei gas e termodinamica
lessons.summary: Temperatura in kelvin, calore e calore latente, legge dei gas perfetti, primo e secondo principio della termodinamica e rendimento delle macchine termiche.

lessons.title: Carica elettrica, campi e circuiti
lessons.summary: Carica, legge di Coulomb, campo e potenziale, legge di Ohm, circuiti in serie e in parallelo e potenza elettrica, con numeri da calcolare a mano.

lessons.title: Magnetismo e induzione elettromagnetica
lessons.summary: Forze magnetiche su cariche in moto e correnti, campi generati dalle correnti, flusso, induzione di Faraday e Lenz, alternatori e trasformatori.

units.title: Matematica
units.summary: La matematica dell’area di fisica e matematica: algebra, funzioni, esponenziali e logaritmi, geometria e trigonometria, probabilità e statistica.

lessons.title: Algebra: equazioni e disequazioni
lessons.summary: Risolvi a mano sistemi lineari, equazioni di secondo grado e disequazioni, usa il discriminante ed evita gli errori di segno che costano punti all’IMAT.

lessons.title: Esponenziali, logaritmi e funzioni
lessons.summary: Usa le proprietà di potenze e logaritmi, risolvi a mano equazioni esponenziali e logaritmiche, e gestisci domini, composizioni, inverse e traslazioni.

lessons.title: Geometria e trigonometria
lessons.summary: Figure piane, cerchi, rette e circonferenze nel piano cartesiano; trigonometria con valori esatti, teoremi dei seni e del coseno e circonferenza goniometrica.

lessons.title: Probabilità e statistica
lessons.summary: Conta i casi, combina le probabilità con le regole di somma, prodotto ed evento contrario, e calcola a mano medie, mediane e medie ponderate.
